name: Inside Out
label: Revelation
lede: Inside Out put out one seven-inch, toured the East Coast once and played a last show in Long Beach in May 1991. The title they'd picked for the second record went with Zack de la Rocha to Los Angeles.

eras.title: A side project finds its singer
eras.text: Inside Out started as a sideline for two guitarists in the Orange County band Hard Stance. A drummer's push and a new guitarist turned it into the band Zack de la Rocha actually sang in, pulling from Minor Threat, Bad Brains, Dag Nasty and, as the songs got heavier, Led Zeppelin.

years.h: Two [[Hard Stance|3029fc29-bf7c-4f78-8bfc-97c0bf144c6d]] guitarists start a band on the side
years.p: [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]] and Rob Haworth both play guitar in Hard Stance. Inside Out is the extra band, with de la Rocha out front on vocals.

years.big: "There was something really sincere in his eyes when he was singing."
years.h: Alex Barreto talks de la Rocha into taking Inside Out seriously
years.p: [[Alex Barreto|9e81a640-5c20-444e-9064-d2d65cf87328]], Hard Stance's drummer, says that of watching de la Rocha sing at Inside Out's first show, near the bottom of a fall 1988 bill. He joins, and pushes the singer to treat it as more than a sideline.
years.xp: De la Rocha had been a guitarist in Hard Stance. Inside Out was the first band where he stood at the mic.

years.h: Vic DiCara arrives from Beyond with riffs to spare
years.p: Fresh from New York's Beyond, [[Vic DiCara|a6698e1f-db17-4e93-9c4f-56678238e91f]] replaces Rob Haworth on guitar, and Inside Out stops sounding like one subgenre. DiCara later said they took a little of everything they liked.
years.xp:
Barreto credited the pairing: "The combination of Zack and Vic was very important and made the band what it was."

Bandcamp Daily describes DiCara's playing as a frenetic style with an endless supply of riffs.

years.h: Rob Haworth's brother takes bass, and a Chain of Strength drummer takes the sticks
years.p: Mark Haworth, another Hard Stance alum, plays bass. [[Chris Bratton|cbaf85ca-1bc7-4eb0-b9cb-ca5d8773b27f]], of [[No for an Answer|23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3]] and [[Chain of Strength|81a3c11e-ac20-4bb4-8614-06b157e802d8]], replaces Barreto on drums before the sessions.
years.xp: Barreto's side of the swap, to Bandcamp Daily: "I was too young to drive!" The older members were tired of driving an hour out of their way to pick him up.

eras.title: Seven inches, one tour
eras.text: A seven-inch, an East Coast run and a radio session are the whole official output. Revelation still calls the record possibly the most popular it has ever put out.

years.cap: De la Rocha at the Unisound, Reading, Pennsylvania, June 28, 1990
years.h: The van dies outside Buffalo, and Jordan Cooper pays for the engine
years.p: Inside Out's one East Coast run is a June package with [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]]'s [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and the new [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]]. Revelation's Jordan Cooper covers the repair.
years.xp:
The tour ran out of New York through Buffalo, Cleveland and City Gardens in New Jersey, with the Unisound in Reading on June 28. Roadie Kevin Egan, the former Beyond singer, wrote it up for No Echo: "I couldn't push the van any faster than 50 miles per hour, then it was 40 miles per hour, then thirty." The engine seized and repairs took five days.

Egan's crew included a young [[Derrick Green|eb624b5f-6580-42d4-af83-19fad8e866ab]], years before he fronted [[Sepultura|1d93c839-22e7-4f76-ad84-d27039efc048]]. Egan also records that he wore no socks the whole tour, and that Shelter arrived by bus.

years.cap: Inside Out on stage in a packed room, around 1990
yt: No Spiritual Surrender, live in Boston, 1990
years.p: Four songs on the original seven-inch, six on the later CD. Revelation calls it possibly its most popular release ever, and says de la Rocha's vocal is as intense as anything on a hardcore record.
years.xp:
Bratton played on the recording, which came just after Mark Haworth joined. Bandcamp Daily calls de la Rocha's vocal on the opener Burning Fight a harrowing and defiant yowl.

The record kept working on later bands: Wikipedia lists [[Refused|42884e27-dfb8-453d-990f-2ffd90bc2d1a]], [[Have Heart|e519e012-e1a3-4592-b3f6-5a16227ab654]], [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]] and even [[Linkin Park|f59c5520-5f46-4d2c-b2c4-822eabf53419]] among those who drew from it.

yt: Live at Loyola Marymount, Los Angeles, 1990
years.h: KXLU, Loyola Marymount's station, gets the songs that came after
years.p: A session on the Los Angeles college station captures Inside Out's unreleased songs at broadcast quality, the best-sounding record of the material written after No Spiritual Surrender.

years.h: "No Spiritual Surrender" live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, June 1990
yt: "No Spiritual Surrender" live at the Anthrax, Norwalk CT, June 1990

eras.title: The last show, and a name that leaves town
eras.text: Vic DiCara's turn to Krishna consciousness ended the band. Left behind was a finished set of new songs, one titled Rage Against the Machine, a name that would be famous by the end of the next year.

years.h: DiCara trades the van for the Krishna temple
years.p: Shortly after No Spiritual Surrender, DiCara joins Cappo's Krishna-conscious Shelter, becomes a Hare Krishna monk, and later starts [[108|7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b]].

years.h: The last show, in Long Beach, plays songs for a second record
years.p: The set includes material meant for that second record, among it Darkness of Greed and one called Rage Against the Machine.

years.h: The unused album title moves to Los Angeles with de la Rocha
years.p: Inside Out is done by the fall. De la Rocha takes the title to Los Angeles, where he, [[Tom Morello|42a636a0-dbe4-4d0c-abe2-1590fad9531b]], [[Tim Commerford|4d61abe3-ce6d-4383-b2cd-8b4491496549]] and [[Brad Wilk|b48aebac-8c3e-48aa-b5e6-2b38f30f5f78]] become [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]].
years.xp:
The planned follow-up to No Spiritual Surrender had a working title, Rage Against the Machine, and a song to match. Neither came out under the Inside Out name. Within a year it was the name of a band signed to Epic.

Mark Haworth went on to State of the Nation, Barreto to Statue.

eras.title: The tape-trader's band
eras.text: With one official record, Inside Out's afterlife has run on bootlegs, surfacing tapes and younger bands. Every few years another piece of the story shows up.

years.p: Oktopus of Dälek turns the title track into Ghost in the Machine for the mashup album Threat: Music That Inspired the Movie.

years.h: Twenty years on, one record store still can't let it go out of stock
years.p: OC Weekly checks in: the EP sells once or twice a week at an Orange County shop, and the manager never lets it run out.
years.xp: OC Weekly's 2010 piece found the seven-inch still moving a couple of times a week, two decades after Revelation No. 19 came out.

years.h: A clean tape of the Long Beach show surfaces
years.p: A high-quality remaster of the May 18, 1991 set appears in February, including the never-released Rage Against the Machine and Darkness of Greed.

yt: Inside Out at the Unisound, Reading, June 28, 1990
years.h: A VHS of the Reading show turns up
years.p: Footage of the June 28, 1990 set at the Unisound in Reading, Pennsylvania, appears online 26 years later.

years.h: Tony Rettman gives the EP an oral history at thirty
years.p: Bandcamp Daily marks the anniversary in July. Barreto's summary: Inside Out had something special, rehearsing or on stage.

years.h: Inside Out's Instagram asks which line-up for 2024
years.p: The account posts Sacrifice with the caption "For 2024 which line up?" and news sites run with it. No public answer followed.
In the Live Lounge, the Baltimore band's Brendan Yates sings the Inside Out song, channeling de la Rocha. It's a song from a band with one EP, on national radio in Britain.
years.xp: Stereogum and setlist.fm point to May 12, 2026 for the performance.
